text:
Shea Theodore's season is a good argument for looking past the scoresheet. He has only six points in 19 games, playing 22 minutes a night, and our wins-added numbers rank him near the bottom of the league because his two goals haven't swung games. Meanwhile, Vegas takes 60% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, nearly 12 points better than when he sits.

That's the Theodore the Golden Knights pay for. Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.5 wins above replacement last season, 46th among defencemen, driving play even after adjusting for teammates and opponents, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 15% of the entries aimed at him (typical 11%). His points pace is below what his talent range suggests, and that usually corrects for a puck-mover who's this good at tilting the ice. With Noah Hanifin out, he's carrying more of the load. Our median for his season is about 37 points; we'd expect the assists to arrive in bunches.
